topics.topic: Whether same-path collisions between unrecognized fields make the request unreadable
questions: Must colliding fields with otherwise unrecognised names make the request unreadable, or must they be left unread without making it unreadable?

Must same-path collisions make the request unreadable only when the path belongs to the CSRF field or an OWNER_FORM_FIELDS row, or must colliding unknown fields cease to be left unread without making the request unreadable?
Must two unknown fields that decode to the same path make the request unreadable, or must unknown fields be ignored before duplicate-path detection?

quotes: when the body or the query cannot be decoded as form fields encoded by the imported TEXT_ENCODING constant, holds two fields whose names _read_form_path reads into the same path (a name given twice among them, or two that differ only in how a position is written), gives a text the row's reads_as cannot read, leaves a gap in a tuple's positions, or when reading body raises, answer the OwnerRequest whose action is the matched row's and every other field None, its = models.OwnerValues with every field None, keeping nothing it partly decoded

These are the only causes: a field whose name is neither the one the imported OWNER_CSRF_FIELD constant names nor one a row of the imported OWNER_FORM_FIELDS constant names MUST be left unread and MUST NOT make the request unreadable, and neither does the query parameter the target is read from, for any method.
judgement.why: The first obligation makes any two fields resolving to the same path render the request unreadable, while the second requires unrecognized fields not to make it unreadable, so two colliding unrecognized fields cannot satisfy both.

topics.topic: Whether duplicate or path-equivalent target query parameters make the request unreadable
questions: Must duplicate or path-equivalent occurrences of the target query parameter make the request unreadable, or is that parameter always excluded from unreadability?
Must repeated or alternatively written target query parameters make the request unreadable, or must the target parameter be excluded from duplicate-path detection?

quotes: when the body or the query cannot be decoded as form fields encoded by the imported TEXT_ENCODING constant, holds two fields whose names _read_form_path reads into the same path (a name given twice among them, or two that differ only in how a position is written), gives a text the row's reads_as cannot read, leaves a gap in a tuple's positions, or when reading body raises, answer the OwnerRequest whose action is the matched row's and every other field None, its = models.OwnerValues with every field None, keeping nothing it partly decoded

These are the only causes: a field whose name is neither the one the imported OWNER_CSRF_FIELD constant names nor one a row of the imported OWNER_FORM_FIELDS constant names MUST be left unread and MUST NOT make the request unreadable, and neither does the query parameter the target is read from, for any method.
judgement.why: The first obligation makes duplicate same-path query fields unreadable without excluding the target parameter, while the second says the target query parameter does not make the request unreadable for any method.

author_guidance: Before editing, identify the decision's owning state from the phase purpose, question_scope and layer obligations, then choose a disposition for each topic that awaits one.
fixed: repair a decision the owning state must make; do not add later-layer implementation choices merely to close a topic. Record the fix commit and review the changed text once.

carried: name the receiving layer and use --what to preserve the choice, its options and consequences, and the required guarantee every option must keep. Decide any guarantee owned here before carrying its execution onward.
accepted: explain why the remaining choice is permitted. Bring an unresolved product choice to the owner with its options and consequences; absence of a quoted requirement does not decide it.
contradiction and standard_violation take no disposition: repair the offending text in its owning state and review the change. Deterministic transition findings must also close through their checks.
